messages:
anna_support: Customer reported invoice INV-2026-0421 discrepancy. Dashboard shows €1,234.56 usage but the invoice line-items sum to €1,234.51 — 0.05 EUR short. Customer is EU VAT-registered and suspects VAT proration / per-request rounding. They attached a CSV export of their dashboard and the invoice PDF.

jose_billing: Can you paste the CSV snippet and an example API request/response or meter entries? Is the dashboard token total matching the meter? :eyes: 

anna_support: Pasted sample meter rows from customer CSV and our meter, and a minimal reproducer: 
```
2026-03-10T12:01:02Z, request_id=abc123, tokens=124, cost_eur=0.2304
2026-03-10T12:01:03Z, request_id=abc124, tokens=3, cost_eur=0.0128
2026-03-10T12:01:04Z, request_id=abc125, tokens=87, cost_eur=0.1617
```
Customer says dashboard shows aggregated total rounded to 2 decimals = €1,234.56 but invoice shows each line rounded to cents then VAT applied per line, resulting in €1,234.51. 

ella_finance: Quick primer: there are two common rounding flows for EU VAT invoices — (A) aggregate net amounts, compute VAT on subtotal, then round; (B) round each line/net VAT individually then sum. Small differences (cents) are expected if the system flips between A and B. We need to know which approach our invoice generator used for this account.

ben_infra: I pulled the billing job run for that invoice (billing-run-20260310-3). Current aggregator (v3.2.1) code is doing per-request rounding before VAT: 
```
// v3.2.1 aggregator snippet
let item_amount = Math.round(request.cost * 100) / 100; // round to cents per request
let vat = Math.round(item_amount * VAT_RATE * 100) / 100;
invoice.addLine(item_amount, vat);
```
That will introduce microcent/millidrifts when many small requests are present. Dashboard sum uses raw meter values and only displays the rounded total, so it looked higher.

jose_billing: That matches customer report. Dashboard aggregate = sum(raw costs) then display-round. Invoice = sum(rounded-per-request + per-line VAT). We should align to invoice-level VAT for EU enterprise invoices to avoid surprising customers.

anna_support: Customer asked for explanation and a fix plan. They requested either a corrected invoice or a credit for the 0.05 EUR immediately.

ella_finance: I'll approve a manual credit for €0.05 against INV-2026-0421. For the longer term, finance prefers approach (A) (aggregate, compute VAT, round once) for EU invoices where legal/regulatory requirements permit — and we should document the behavior clearly in billing docs.

ben_infra: Creating engineering ticket BL-8421 to update aggregation semantics: compute subtotal in integer micros (or high-precision decimals), sum across requests, compute VAT on subtotal, then round the final VAT and total once. Add a feature flag to preserve legacy per-request rounding for existing tenants that rely on it.

billing-bot: Ticket BL-8421 created by ben_infra. Priority: P2. https://redwood.internal/issue/BL-8421

jose_billing: QA plan: generate a staging invoice with many small request rows across EU VAT accounts, compare (dashboard_display_rounded_total) vs (invoice_total) and assert diff <= 0.01 EUR. If good, ship behind flag, run for two billing cycles, then flip for impacted customers.

anna_support: I notified the customer: explained root cause (per-request rounding + per-line VAT), told them we issued a €0.05 credit and opened BL-8421. They asked for ETA — gave an estimated timeline of 2 sprints. Customer acknowledged and is satisfied for now. :white_check_mark: 

ella_finance: Filed internal note to record manual journal entry: credit_label=rounding-correction, amount=0.05 EUR, invoice=INV-2026-0421, authorized_by=ella_finance.

ben_infra: Follow-ups: 1) implement aggregation change, 2) add end-to-end integration tests comparing dashboard vs invoice generation, 3) update billing docs to call out rounding policy per region.

anna_support: Closing support thread once customer confirms receipt of the credit. Will re-open if they see any further discrepancies.
